title: Bioinformatics
description: Bioinformatics analysis methods and programming skills. Practical bioinformatic software for sequence analysis, bioinformatic algorithms and programming fundamentals.

title: Special Topics in Bioinformatics and Medical Informatics
description: Advanced selected topics in bioinformatics and medical informatics.

title: Computational Genomics and Bioinformatics
description: Biological and genomic data. Application of computational algorithms to biological questions. Post-genomic techniques in annotation and comparison of microbial and eukaryotic genome sequences.

title: Population Genetics
description: Theoretical and applied population genetics to include genetic diversity in natural populations, random drift, mutation, gene flow, natural selection, nucleotide variation, and quantitative genetics. Emphasis on data analysis and interpretation.

title: Advanced Topics in Bioinformatics and Medical Informatics
description: Recent technological developments and scientific breakthroughs that have a changing effect on the field of biomedical informatics.

title: Phylogenetic Systematics
description: Theory and methodology of phylogenetic systematics. Includes use of computer algorithms, survey of literature and preparation of a project in phylogenetic systematics.

title: Selected Topics in Bioinformatics and Medical Informatics
description: Intensive study in specific areas of biological or medical informatics. In-depth investigation of specific challenges in the field as well as introduction to current and emerging technologies.

title: Research
description: Research in one of the fields of bioinformatics and medical informatics.

title: Thesis or Project
description: Preparation of a project or thesis for the master’s degree.

title: Thesis Extension
description: Registration required in any semester or term following assignment of RP in Course 799A in which the student expects to use the facilities and resources of the university; also student must be registered in the course when the completed thesis is granted final approval.
